segments.line: Then, on Tuesday, you go to
the bank with your mum. At
the counter, there's an old lady from down your road, Mrs. Hale. Her number is eighteen thousand dollars. Her whole life's savings.
Next to her is a nice young man in a nice jacket, helping her with a form.
'Just sign here, and your money will be safe. ' His number is minus ninety thousand.
She signs.
And you watch it happen.
Her number drops. Eighteen thousand. Nine thousand. Zero. And
his number jumps by the exact same amount, at the exact same second.
You shout before you can think. 'Stop him! '
Security grabs him at the door. The bank
freezes the transfer. Mrs. Hale gets every cent back.
She hugs you and won't let go. The
manager wants your name. A local reporter takes your picture. You tell everyone you just had a bad feeling about him.
In America alone, people reported losing more than ten billion dollars to fraud in one year. That's real.
And nobody else in that bank saw it happen.
But somebody saw you.
The next morning, there's a man in a grey suit at the school gate.
'You knew, ' he says. 'Before the bank did. Before anyone. How? ' You
look at the space above his head. And for the first time, something is wrong with a number.
It just says zero. Exactly zero.
A man in a suit that perfect, with nothing at all. As if he doesn't exist.
